newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO says H1 profit talk groundless.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO says H1 profit talk groundless.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Monday rumours that its first half results would be at least 30 percent higher than a year ago were groundless.
Spokesman Jules Prast said a news report which sparked the talk, which circulated in the market last week, based its claims on an anonymous source within the Dutch bank.
But he said this was impossible.
"There are no such figures available yet. It's a totally groundless rumour," Prast told Reuters.
"We don't have the numbers yet, so how can anybody else have them."
ABN AMRO is due to issue its results for the first half of 1997 on August 21.
The bank earned a net profit of 1.70 billion guilders in the first half of 1996, up 36 percent on a year earlier.
ABN AMRO shares rose on Friday on the rumours.
